correctness.rationale: For every integer \(j\ge3\) and cut \(m,b\ge 2^j-1\), Lucas congruence makes the computational-basis coefficient sign depend only on the sum of Hamming-weight residues modulo \(q=2^j\). Orthonormal residue compression gives the exact matrix \(T\) and all positive eigenvalues of \(TT^{\mathsf T}\). Its factor \(F=J-2R\) satisfies \(FF^{\mathsf T}=4I+(q-4)J\), with positive eigenvalues \((q-2)^2\) and \(4\), proving rank \(q\). A roots-of-unity filter proves fixed-\(q\) convergence of both residue distributions to uniform, giving one eigenvalue \((1-2/q)^2\) and \(q-1\) eigenvalues \(4/q^2\); entropy is \(O((\log q)/q)\), while Schmidt rank \(q\) diverges. Actual standalone checker passed 21 separate normalization, direct small-state spectrum, rank and limiting-spectrum comparisons. Exact proof, not finite testing, supports the infinite family. No assertion for uniform joint limits or other arities.

value.rationale: A natural complete hypergraph-state family exhibits exact Schmidt rank \(q\) for every qualifying finite cut but sequential limiting von Neumann entropy tending to zero as \(q\) grows. The complete finite Schmidt spectrum, limiting rank-one-dominant law and purity are structurally useful quantum many-body benchmarks. This is an infinite all-parameter statement, not an isolated computation or an unsupported numerical improvement. The qualitative separation of Schmidt rank from entropic entanglement survives all \(q=2^j\), \(j\ge3\).
